Effects of Quirk Suppression.text: When a Quirk is suppressed, the power stops at its source, but whatever it already did stays done. An Emitter stops producing its effect at once: no new flame, current or force comes out. A fire it already lit keeps burning, a thrown object keeps flying and an object it already created stays real. Effects that need the user's continued power, such as a held barrier, a floating load, a moving shadow or a grip that keeps something in place, collapse the moment suppression lands, which makes suppressing a user in midair or under a heavy load dangerous. A Transformation ends and the body returns to its normal form. A Mutant body does not change at all: gills, wings, claws, strength and senses that are part of the body stay, because they are anatomy, not a power being switched on. A suppressed person feels the Quirk go silent and gets it back with no lasting harm when the suppression ends. Suppression never touches training, weapons, gear or plain muscle, so a suppressed fighter can still fight. Erasure-type Quirks, restraint devices and suppression gear all follow this rule, and heroes and officers plan for what remains after the power is gone.
